prompt: Where TOGAF's centre is a process, what is IAF's centre?
hint: Rows and columns.

choices.text: A notation for drawing enterprise models
choices.why: IAF has no notation of its own; ArchiMate or any other can be used.

choices.text: A grid of levels and aspect areas
choices.why: Right: four questions asked of four parts of the enterprise, with security and governance across them.

choices.text: A certification programme
choices.why: IAF has only a small certification market; that is not its centre.

choices.text: A cycle of eight phases around a centre
choices.why: That is TOGAF's ADM.

prompt: Which common failure does IAF's rule of answering the levels in order catch?
hint: Starting at the bottom row.

choices.text: Product first, reasons after
choices.why: Yes: in the grid, a decision with nothing above it in its column is visibly floating.

choices.text: Skipping the governance band
choices.why: Governance matters, but the ordering rule is about the levels.

choices.text: Drawing too many diagrams
choices.why: The rule is about justification, not quantity.

choices.text: Writing requirements before reasons
choices.why: That is close, and still not the failure the lesson names: the product chosen first.

prompt: Match each IAF level to its question.
hint: In order, from the top.

prompt: Match each part of Carcará's digital boarding to its IAF level.
hint: No product is named above the physical level.

pairs.left: every passenger boards with a digital ticket by 2027
a validation service that answers within a second, network or not
a validation component on the driver's device with a per-trip list
the boarding app on Android with SQLite

prompt: The phones may be replaced by handheld validators in 2028. Which level of the design stays true?
hint: Logical is what; physical is which product.

choices.text: Physical, since the app will be rewritten anyway
choices.why: The physical level is exactly what changes with the device.

choices.text: Neither; the whole column gets redone
choices.why: That is what the logical level prevents.

choices.text: The logical one
choices.why: Right: a validation component on the driver's device with a per-trip list, whatever the device is.

choices.text: The contextual level alone
choices.why: The conceptual and logical levels survive too; only the physical one moves.

prompt: IAF keeps information as an area separate from information systems. What did that find at Carcará?
hint: What is a ticket?

choices.text: That ticketing and Frota use different databases
choices.why: Known already, and a systems fact, not an information one.

choices.text: Sales and Finance meant different things by a ticket
choices.why: Yes: a seat for one, a revenue line for the other, both built into systems unnoticed.

choices.text: That passenger data was stored abroad
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: That the boarding app needed a new data model
choices.why: A design detail, not what separating information revealed.

prompt: Why does the lesson draw security as a band across all the levels rather than a column?
hint: A product bought with no reasons above it.

choices.text: Because security belongs to the technology team
choices.why: The band says the opposite: it belongs at every level.

choices.text: Because the LGPD requires that layout
choices.why: The law does not prescribe diagrams.

choices.text: It is decided at each level
choices.why: Right: a security decision made only at the physical level is missing its reasons.

choices.text: To save space on the page
choices.why: The layout carries a claim about where decisions are made.

prompt: This is IAF's grid without its words. Put each level's name on its row, and mark the security band.
hint: The order runs from the reason down to the product.

prompt: Match each IAF level to where it maps in TOGAF, by the lesson.
hint: Vision first, products in phase E.

prompt: How did Tainá combine the two frameworks in Carcará's phase C?
hint: One gives the cycle, the other the headings.

choices.text: She replaced the ADM with IAF's grid
choices.why: She kept the ADM; the grid organised the content of one phase.

choices.text: IAF's levels became the headings inside the phase
choices.why: Yes: the conceptual and logical levels kept product choices out until phase E.

choices.text: She produced two separate documents, one per framework
choices.why: Two documents of one decision drift apart; she used one.

choices.text: She used IAF for security and nothing else
choices.why: Security is one band; she used the levels.

prompt: Match each ArchiMate relationship to what it means.
hint: Serving provides; realisation brings into being.

pairs.right: an element provides its functionality to another
an element brings a more abstract one into being
who or what performs a behaviour
a behaviour reads or writes a passive element

right_distractors: an element is deployed in a region

prompt: What are ArchiMate's three core layers?
hint: The same as three of TOGAF's domains.

choices.text: Business, application and technology
choices.why: Right, with motivation, strategy and migration elements around them.

choices.text: Context, containers and components
choices.why: Those are C4's levels.

choices.text: Contextual, conceptual and logical
choices.why: Those are IAF's levels.

choices.text: Structure, behaviour and interaction
choices.why: Close to ArchiMate's aspects, which are a different axis from its layers.

prompt: For one system's engineering team, what does the lesson prefer to ArchiMate?
hint: Less vocabulary for the same need.

choices.text: BPMN for each diagram
choices.why: BPMN is for processes, not for the structure of a system.

choices.text: C4 and UML
choices.why: Yes: they say what an engineering team needs with less vocabulary; ArchiMate suits the enterprise view.

choices.text: No diagrams
choices.why: Lesson 1 argued for diagrams that answer questions, not for none.

choices.text: The IAF grid
choices.why: The grid organises content; it is not a notation.

prompt: Match each framework to who made it or what it is for.
hint: Government, defence, alliance, one system.

pairs.right: NATO, which replaced MODAF for the UK
a template for one system's architecture

prompt: What problem do the government and defence frameworks share, by the lesson?
hint: Why is their size justified for them and not for Carcará?

choices.text: They protect classified information
choices.why: True of some, and not the shared problem that explains their weight.

choices.text: Their systems are older than most companies'
choices.why: Age is not what the lesson gives.

choices.text: They are maintained by public bodies
choices.why: Who maintains them does not explain their size.

choices.text: Many parties' descriptions must combine
choices.why: Right: many organisations or suppliers must produce descriptions that can be compared and combined.

prompt: Match each example to the kind of thing called a framework.
hint: Method, taxonomy, notation.

prompt: Every team at a company draws its container diagrams differently. What helps, by the lesson's table?
hint: A notation and one page.

choices.text: Adopting TOGAF's full content framework
choices.why: That adds many deliverables and does not settle how anybody draws.

choices.text: A notation and a how-we-draw page
choices.why: Yes: C4 for systems, ArchiMate for the enterprise view.

choices.text: DoDAF viewpoints
choices.why: They solve the many-suppliers problem, not a team's drawing habits.

choices.text: More reviews of each diagram before it is published
choices.why: Reviews catch inconsistencies; a shared convention prevents them.

prompt: A public tender requires TOGAF deliverables, and the team works with C4, decision records and scenarios. What does the lesson advise?
hint: Two descriptions drift.

choices.text: Switch the team to TOGAF artefacts for good
choices.why: That throws away the descriptions the team actually uses.

choices.text: Map what the team uses into the required format
choices.why: Right: keep the decisions where they live and render them into what is required.

choices.text: Refuse the tender
choices.why: Not necessary; the requirement can be met.

choices.text: Keep two parallel sets and update both
choices.why: Two descriptions of one system drift apart.

prompt: A manager asks: should we use TOGAF or ArchiMate? What is the best answer from this lesson?
hint: Are they the same kind of thing?

choices.text: TOGAF, as it is the larger standard
choices.why: Size is not the issue; they do different jobs.

choices.text: ArchiMate, as it is newer
choices.why: Age does not decide it either.

choices.text: Neither; use IAF
choices.why: IAF is a third kind of thing, a taxonomy.

choices.text: They differ in kind; use both
choices.why: Yes: a method and a notation, which combine.

prompt: IAF's four levels ask why, what, how and with what; the level that asks how, without naming products, is the ___ level.
hint: Between conceptual and physical.
